title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RC_---0LD_0LE0RF_1RE0RA_0LF1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RC_---0LD_0LE0RF_1RE0RA_0LF1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is almost all 1s: a few long solid blocks separated by single 0s. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) finds no halt in the first 1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 2,359 cells have been visited and 2,352 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.318).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) runs 1012 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Cutting in the ratio 3 : 1
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell on the left, between steps 8.68·10<sup>7</sup> and 8.85·10<sup>7</sup>, the first solid block went 997, 744, 557, 414, 391, 394, the cut-off pieces being 248, 187, 138: each cut keeps about three quarters.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state C was entered 16,645,884 times, always reading a 1 (C0 halts).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a few long solid blocks separated by single 0s; at the left end the first block is cut in the ratio 3 : 1 again and again, and at the right end the blocks are merged back into two.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells).
The first block is cut again and again, keeping about three quarters each time.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 2,359 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With b for 110, so that 1^n b is n + 2 ones and a 0, around step 8.7·107:

At the left end the first block is cut again and again in the ratio about 3 : 1: 997 into 744 and 248, 744 into 557 and 187, 557 into 414 and 138. A cut needs passes over the block, which is where the time goes. When the cutting stops the head runs to the right end and the blocks are merged into two (1^573 b 1^501), and the next round starts. The tape grows by a few cells per round; the width grows like a power of the step count near 1/3 (fitted 0.34 and 0.32 for the two sides at 109 steps).

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is C reading a 0. C is entered from B, reading 0 (1LC) or 1 (0RC). In the first 108 steps C was entered 16,645,884 times, every time on a 1, and 16,640,969 times at least 7 cells from the left end. A halt needs B to read a 0 or a 1 and then find a 0 where it lands: 0 B>0 or B>1 0, which never happened in the first 108 steps.
Whether the cutting and merging ever produce that pattern is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.318).
After 109 steps the tape spans 2,359 cells (1,106 left of the start, 819 right), with a density of 1s of 0.997.
